proposals.expected_failure_mode: May underfit timing if admissions systematically lag infections; peak timing could be slightly early relative to hospitalization-rate target.
proposals.rationale: Baseline SEIR in the SEIR family with direct I observation to keep identifiability strong in a short, single-season series; can accommodate sharp peaks via implicit time-varying transmission/forcing without adding compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Lag may be weakly identified and behave like a redundant degree of freedom; could drift across rolling splits if true lag varies within season.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior best spec and surveillance note that admissions may lag an I-state proxy; 1-week lag is a parsimonious way to align peak timing without adding compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Risk of over-shifting peaks and degrading early-season fit; may compensate by distorting latent dynamics, reducing stability.
proposals.rationale: Explores modest lag uncertainty (0–2 weeks) while staying within SEIR; a 2-week delay can better align hospitalization peaks if clinical/reporting delays are longer in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Waning parameter may be poorly identified in a single season and can introduce spurious oscillation/over-flexibility, harming rolling stability.
proposals.rationale: Adds waning immunity to allow sharper, more transient peaks without introducing hospitalization compartment; still parsimonious and within SEIR-family extensions.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Fractional dynamics can be harder to identify and may blur interpretability; could over-smooth or mis-time peaks if memory effect is not supported by data.
proposals.rationale: Fractional SEIR can represent heavy-tailed dwell times/effective memory, which may help capture high peakiness without extra compartments; keeps observation simple to avoid delay+structure confounding.
